audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer gave LeBlanc all seven stages — the packet itself flags this as a defect ('LeBlanc wins only 46.65% but the chart gives LeBlanc 7/7'). The full layer already read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Malzahar/Skill/Malzahar. whys[2] even argued that the phase 'favors him' while win[2] said LeBlanc.
audit.why: Malzahar's Void Shift gives damage reduction and CC immunity until he takes damage, Call of the Void is a 900-range silence on a flat 6s, and Nether Grasp is a 700-range suppression. None of that loses a lane 7/7.
audit.corrected: win[0..3] -> Skill, win[4] -> Malzahar, win[5] -> Skill, win[6] -> Malzahar, matching the full layer, with all seven whys rewritten to argue their rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike named 'Netherworld ult'. His ultimate is Nether Grasp. The first-item and late spikes also treated his scaling as irrelevant when Nether Grasp drops from 140 seconds to 80.
audit.corrected: spikes[1], whys[4..6], phases[4].why and phases[6].why rewritten with the real name and the 140-to-80 second curve.

audit.whatIsWrong: Call of the Void was called a root in five places. It is a SILENCE. Against LeBlanc that distinction is the entire matchup: a root still lets you press Distortion's return, a silence does not — you die on the spot he landed you. Separately, Nether Grasp is a channel that Ethereal Chains cancels, and Void Shift is damage reduction plus CC immunity, not a 'passive shield'.
audit.why: Enemy Q text: 'deal Magic Damage and silence enemy champions'. Enemy R is flagged channel. Enemy passive: 'massive damage reduction and crowd control immunity'. missingInteractions lists silence-denies-answer and channel-interruptible.
audit.corrected: early, mid, spikes[1], phases[0..3].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d and wants.you[2] all now say silence, name Void Shift correctly, and tell you to hold E to break the channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and early claimed a whiffed Call of the Void leaves him 'defenseless until it's back up nearly ten seconds later'. It is a flat 6 seconds.
audit.why: Enemy Q cooldown 6, flat. E 11/10/9/8/7. W 8. R 140/110/80.
audit.corrected: Both corrected; the punishable window is now stated as the 6-second Q and the 140-second rank-1 ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles, and dontsFull[1].t called his kit 'his one CC spell' when he has two distinct forms of it.
audit.why: lintFindings COPY_PASTE_BLEED on both bullets; enemy Q silences and enemy R suppresses.
audit.corrected: Both bullets replaced with kit-grounded bodies; the don't title now names the 900-range Q.

edits.before: - Malzahar Nether Grasp: matchup-defining — Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Distortion (return) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Nether Grasp is 140s at rank 1, 80s at rank 3, and it is a channel: Ethereal Chains or a mimicked chain breaks the suppression. - Call of the Void is a flat 6s silence at 900 range — if it lands first, your W return does not exist. - Malefic Visions is 11s down to 7s.

edits.before: Malzahar's Void Swarm minions and Malefic Visions dots make early trading annoying since he can poke you passively while farming, and Call of the Void is a straight skillshot that punishes predictable dashes. Still, he has zero mobility and no way to escape once you're in Sigil range, so patient play — waiting out his poke, then engaging when Void is down — wins trades comfortably. Your clone lets you bait the root safely, and once it whiffs he's defenseless until it's back up nearly ten seconds later.
edits.after: Malzahar's Void Swarm minions and Malefic Visions make early trading annoying, since Visions ticks for 11 seconds and refreshes whenever he casts anything else on you. Call of the Void is a 900-range skillshot that silences — not roots — so it does not hold you, it takes your W return away. Void Shift also gives him damage reduction and CC immunity until he has taken damage, so chip first, then commit. His Q is only 6 seconds, so a whiff is a short window, not a free lane.

edits.before: Level 6 is the one phase where Malzahar can flip a fight: if he lands Call of the Void into Netherworld suppress, you cannot flash or blink out and he can delete you with allied follow-up. Because of this, never all-in him blind past 6 — bait the root with the clone first, exactly as you would pre-6, and only commit the real combo once it's spent. Outside of that specific root-into-ult window, you still hold every tempo and burst advantage and can freely roam since he has no gap-closer to punish your rotations.
edits.after: Level 6 is where Malzahar flips the lane: Nether Grasp is a 700-range suppression on 140 seconds at rank 1, and if Call of the Void silences you first, Distortion's return is unavailable and you die where you landed. Never all-in him blind past 6 — bait the silence with the clone, then commit once it is spent. But Nether Grasp is a channel: Ethereal Chains, or a mimicked chain, breaks it outright, which is the one answer his kit has no reply to. Hold E for that, not for the wave.

edits.before: Force all-ins only after baiting his Void Swarm minions or his root
edits.after: Force all-ins only after baiting the Call of the Void silence

notes: The packet itself flagged the content chart as contradicting the win rate, so win[] was moved to match the full layer; no phases[].side edits were needed. The largest correction here is conceptual: five fields called Call of the Void a root. It is a silence, and against LeBlanc specifically that means Distortion's return is unavailable rather than merely delayed — the difference between a survivable trade and a death. Malefic Visions' spread-on-death is in Riot's text but its trigger is the target dying, not an HP threshold, so I did not write the missingInteractions 'execute-threshold' framing as a threshold number.
